enriched_description: Historical sailing vessel characterized by two or more masts with the foremast shorter than or equal to the mainmast, rigged primarily with fore-and-aft sails (gaff-rigged or Bermuda-rigged). Hull is constructed from wooden planking or steel with a sleek, narrow profile optimized for speed. Length ranges from 15 to 50 meters. Features include a bowsprit extending forward, multiple staysails between masts, and a gaff-rigged mainsail with a distinctive four-sided shape. Deck includes a raised cabin or deckhouse, steering wheel or tiller, and rigging lines. Distinguishing features include fore-and-aft sail configuration, multiple masts with foremast shorter than main, and classic sailing vessel hull form.

Large display board for showing contest scores and game information, mounted at a prominent location in a sports venue. Traditional variants are rectangular panels (2-10 meters wide) with manually operated number tiles or flip-card mechanisms. Electronic variants feature LED or LCD displays with pixel matrices showing scores, time, and statistics in bright, high-contrast characters. Frame is constructed from metal with a dark background for visibility. May include team logos, sponsor branding, and multiple information zones. Distinguishing features include large-scale display format, score-oriented information layout, and venue-mounted installation.

Display surface of a cathode-ray tube (CRT) monitor or television, characterized by a slightly convex glass face with a phosphor-coated interior. Screen area is rectangular (4:3 aspect ratio typical), 20-50 cm diagonally, surrounded by a dark bezel or frame. Surface exhibits a slight curvature (bubble effect) characteristic of CRT technology. When active, displays images composed of scanned electron beam lines with visible scan lines at close inspection. Glass surface has a slight greenish or grayish tint. Distinguishing features include convex glass face, CRT bezel surround, and characteristic phosphor display surface.

Threaded fastener consisting of a cylindrical shank with a helical ridge (thread) and a head with a drive recess. Shank diameter ranges from 2-12 mm, length from 5-100 mm. Head types include flat (countersunk), pan, round, or hex, with drive recesses such as slotted, Phillips, Torx, or hex socket. Material is steel, stainless steel, brass, or aluminum with zinc, chrome, or black oxide finish. Thread pitch varies by application (coarse for wood, fine for metal). Distinguishing features include helical thread pattern, drive-recess head, and tapered or blunt shank geometry.

Hand tool for driving screws, consisting of a handle, a metal shaft, and a tip shaped to fit into a screw head recess. Handle is molded plastic, rubber, or wood, 8-12 cm long, with an ergonomic grip profile and hanging hole. Shaft is hardened steel, 5-20 cm long, with a smooth or knurled surface. Tip is flat (slotted), cross-shaped (Phillips), star-shaped (Torx), or hexagonal, precision-ground to match screw recess dimensions. Overall length 15-30 cm. Distinguishing features include elongated metal shaft, shaped drive tip, and ergonomic handle grip.

Safety restraint system consisting of a woven nylon webbing strap (4-5 cm wide) with a metal buckle and latch plate mechanism. Lap belt variant is a single strap across the hips; three-point variant includes a shoulder strap crossing the chest diagonally. Webbing is black, gray, or colored with a tightly woven texture. Buckle is a rectangular metal housing with a red release button. Retractor mechanism is housed in a plastic casing mounted to the vehicle frame. Distinguishing features include woven webbing strap, metal buckle with release button, and vehicle-mounted restraint configuration.

Home appliance for stitching fabric, consisting of a horizontal arm extending from a vertical body with a needle bar, presser foot, and bobbin mechanism. Body is constructed from cast metal and plastic, typically 35-45 cm wide, 20-30 cm deep, and 25-35 cm tall. Needle moves vertically through the fabric, interlocking with a rotating bobbin thread below. Control features include a foot pedal for speed, stitch selection dial, and tension adjustment. Surface is painted white, gray, or black with brand markings. Distinguishing features include horizontal sewing arm, vertical needle mechanism, presser foot assembly, and bobbin housing.

Defensive armor piece carried on the arm to intercept blows, constructed from wood, metal, leather, or composite materials. Shape varies by type: round (hoplon, Viking), kite-shaped (Norman), heater-shaped (medieval), or rectangular (riot shield). Dimensions range from 40-100 cm in height. Surface may be painted, embossed, or decorated with heraldic emblems, crosses, or geometric patterns. Back features arm straps (enarmes) and a central grip (umbo) for holding. Metal shields exhibit a hammered or polished finish; wooden shields show grain and painted decoration. Distinguishing features include arm-mounted configuration, defensive curvature, and heraldic or decorative surface treatment.

Retail establishment specializing in footwear sales, characterized by a storefront with large display windows showcasing shoes on mannequin feet or shelves. Interior features wall-mounted shelving units, display racks, and seating areas for trying on shoes. Shoe boxes are stacked on shelves behind the counter or in storage areas. Lighting is bright and focused on merchandise. Signage displays brand names and store logo. Floor is typically hard surface (tile, wood, or laminate) for easy cleaning. Distinguishing features include footwear display arrangements, shoe box storage, and retail fitting area.

Traditional Japanese sliding partition consisting of a wooden lattice frame covered with translucent washi (rice paper). Frame is constructed from light-colored wood (cedar, cypress, or hinoki) with a grid pattern of thin wooden slats (kumiko) creating rectangular or geometric openings. Paper is hand-made washi, off-white or cream-colored, stretched taut across the frame and adhered to the back of the lattice. Dimensions match standard Japanese room modules (approximately 90 x 180 cm per panel). Slides in a wooden track (kamoi and shikii). Distinguishing features include wooden lattice grid, translucent paper surface, and sliding panel configuration.
